seo.title: TablePro vs HeidiSQL: databases, platforms and pricing
seo.description: HeidiSQL is free on Windows, Linux and, since 2026, Apple silicon Macs. TablePro is native on Mac, iPhone and iPad. Compare databases, builds and prices.

header.title: TablePro vs HeidiSQL
header.lead: HeidiSQL and TablePro are open-source database clients with different engine and platform support. HeidiSQL has no paid plans; TablePro charges for optional features.

tablepro: An official Intel Mac build, as well as Apple silicon.
MongoDB, Redis, ClickHouse or DuckDB alongside SQL servers.
Free AI chat and MCP, plus a separate iPhone and iPad app.
competitor: The same free client on Windows, Linux and Apple silicon Macs.
Every feature free, with no paid plans.

glance.intro: HeidiSQL’s Mac build has been attached to every release since version {cells.macBuild.version}, published {cells.macBuild.date}. It runs on Apple silicon only.

macBuild.label: Mac build
macBuild.tablepro: Separate builds for Apple silicon and Intel

items.text: It connects to Firebird, Interbase and ProxySQL, which TablePro does not support.
It is free and open source under the GPL, with no paid plans.
TablePro runs on Intel Macs as well as Apple silicon, with a separate build for each. HeidiSQL’s Mac build is for Apple silicon only.
Besides SQL databases, it connects to MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DuckDB and other engines, each with its own way to query. See the <link>supported databases</link>.
Passwords stay in the macOS Keychain, and a connection’s <link>Safe Mode</link> level can ask for Touch ID or your password before a write runs.
The <link>AI assistant and the MCP server</link> are free in the Mac app, with the AI provider you choose.
A free <link>iPhone and iPad app</link> connects to MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server and SQLite, among others.
Firebird, Interbase and ProxySQL are not among the supported engines.
Some features are paid. Starter adds features such as {starterExamples}, while HeidiSQL has no paid plans.

switching.intro: TablePro has no importer for HeidiSQL. Add each session as a TablePro connection: fill in the connection form, or paste a URL that starts with mysql://, postgresql:// or sqlserver:// into <ui>File > Import > Import from URL…</ui>
after: Set up an SSH tunnel on the connection’s <ui>Network</ui> tab. On the Mac, jump hosts are supported too.
Passwords go into the macOS Keychain.
Query history starts fresh in TablePro.

faq.question: Do I still need Wine to run HeidiSQL on a Mac?
faq.answer: No, not on a Mac with Apple silicon. Since version {cells.macBuild.version}, HeidiSQL publishes a Mac app for Apple silicon. It has no Mac build for Intel processors.

faq.question: Which databases do both clients cover?
faq.answer: HeidiSQL’s site lists MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, SQLite and Redshift, and TablePro supports all of them. HeidiSQL adds Firebird, Interbase and ProxySQL. TablePro adds document, key-value and analytical engines such as MongoDB, Redis and ClickHouse.

notes.heidisql-delphi-on-windows: The Windows version is built with Delphi
notes.heidisql-databases: MariaDB, MySQL, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Interbase, Firebird, ProxySQL and Redshift, as its site lists them
notes.heidisql-mac-arm64-only: A signed and notarized app for Apple silicon. There is no build for Intel Macs.
